REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 10, 2020 -
07:00 P.M.
TELECONFERENCE MEETING AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20 VIA ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID #859 5040 6002
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, the City Council Chamber and City Hall are closed to the public. Consistent with State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the Los Angeles County Health Officer’s “Safer at Home Order for Control of COVID-19” the City Council will participate in the meeting through teleconference. Public participation in the meeting will be facilitated through the electronic methods as described below.
Agenda Materials:
The agenda and agenda packet related to items on this agenda are available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet will be made available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION:
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us and on Cerritos TV3.
Public Comments:
Members of the public may provide public comment through the following methods:
Email: Members of the public may provide public comment by submitting an email to city_clerk@cerritos.us by 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the meeting date and agenda item number for which you would like to provide comment in the subject line of the email. The public comment will be distributed to all members of the City Council. During the meeting your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: You may provide audio public comment by connecting to the teleconference meeting online or by telephone/mobile call (please select only one method). Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time on the agenda. You must be available to provide comment at the time you are called upon to speak. If you are not planning on providing public comment we encourage you to observe the meeting via livestream or on Cerritos TV3 to allow staff to more effectively manage the number of teleconference connections.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85950406002
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 859 5040 6002
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations:
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 10, 2020, 7:00 P.M., TELECONFERENCED MEETING
AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20,
VIA ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 859 5040 6002

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council as follows:

  Cerritos Community College (65th anniversary – September 17, 2020).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Jose Fierro, representing Cerritos Community College, thanked the City Council for
  issuing a proclamation to the College in honor of their upcoming 65th Anniversary.

  Kent Galante, representing Sheraton Cerritos, expressed concern with the City Council’s
  action to increase commercial waste management rates.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August 27,
  2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  September 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August 27, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September 10, 2020
  (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration by
  Councilmember Hu.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of
  Demands, as follows:

  City of Cerritos  9/10/2020  $ 6,510,009.67 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Hu
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City & Theater Marketing Manager/City
  Librarian. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.
 City of Cerritos  September 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration of expanding the existing level of service provided by the
  Cerritos Electric Utility (CEU) to include residential customers (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ramzi Raufdeen, Electric Utility Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Mel Cortez inquired as to whom the public may call for assistance with services, if
  additional staff will be required and what expense to the City this could incur, and if fees
  will be charged to those who qualify for the program.

  Gail Grossman inquired as to whether or not the public is mandated to sign up for the
  program, if a “level” pay plan will be available, and whether there is a medical usage
  program, such as is offered by Southern California Edison.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MAIN MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Approve Option No. 1, with the following criteria for selection of residential
  customers:

  a.  Expand the existing level of service provided by the Cerritos Electric
  Utility (CEU) to include residential customers; and

  b.  Criteria for selection of residential customers: “First come, first served”
  basis (COUNCIL).

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION TO MAIN MOTION (VOTE): It was moved by Barrows, and
  seconded by Vo, to make a substitute motion to the main motion made by Yokoyama,
  to:

  1.  Approve Option No. 1, expand the existing level of service provided by the
  Cerritos Electric Utility (CEU) to include residential customers and direct the City
  Manager to include a review of the City’s residential participation in the Cerritos
  Electric Utility during the annual review of the City’s proposed fiscal year budget;
  and

  2.  Vote separately on any proposed criteria for the selection of residential
  customers (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  September 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  Councilmember Yokoyama requested a motion to reconsider the vote on the substitute
  motion made by Councilmember Barrows, in order to change his “no” vote to “yes,”
  stating that it was his understanding that the substitute motion question placed before
  the City Council was whether the City Council should take a separate vote on expanding
  the existing level of services provided by the Cerritos Electric Utility (CEU) to include
  residential customers and a separate vote on the criteria for selecting residential
  customers. Seeing that there was no motion from the members of the prevailing side of
  the substitute motion to reconsider the vote, the substitute motion carried pursuant to
  the original (4 – 1) vote.

  VOTE ON REMAINDER OF MAIN MOTION (DID NOT CARRY): It was moved by
  Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to approve the criteria for the selection of residential
  customers to be served by the Cerritos Electric Utility, as follows:

  1.  Criteria for selection of residential customers: “First come, first served” basis
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion did not carry (2 -3) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama
  NOES:  Barrows, Vo, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the criteria for the
  selection of residential customers to be served by the Cerritos Electric Utility, in the
  following priority order:

  1.  Serve qualifying low-income senior and/or disabled residents

  2.  Serve qualifying low-income and/or disabled residents on a “first come, first
  served” basis

  3.  Serve residents on a “first come, first served” basis

  4.  Serve residents based on a lottery selection process (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of award of contract for South Street rehabilitation, Project
  No. 21301, Bid No. 1405-20 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  September 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $172,390.00 for South Street Rehabilitation (base
  bid and alternates #2 and #3), Project No. 21301, Bid No. 1405-20, to COPP
  Contracting, Inc. and reject the other bids; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmember Barrows and Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem Vo
  and Mayor Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager/City Clerk to facilitate the
  processes and procedures to begin conducting City Council meetings in the Council
  Chamber by the first meeting in October 2020.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to waive the $1,000,000 liability
  insurance requirement for the upcoming Cerritos Iron-Wood Women’s Golf Club event,
  research the insurance requirements of other cities for similar events/groups, and
  provide the information to either the Parks and Recreation Commission or the City
  Council.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to conduct the annual Dr. Martin
  Luther King, Jr. Day Ceremony in either a live outdoor or virtual setting, in accordance
  with the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, in January 2021.
 City of Cerritos  September 10, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session to discuss the items listed on the
  Closed Session agenda.

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Manager

12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Clerk/Treasurer

12D. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6 (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Art Gallucci, Patricia Leyva, and Charles Goldstein
  Employee Organization: AFSCME, Local 619

12E.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6 (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Art Gallucci and Charles Goldstein
  Unrepresented Employees: Full-Time Exempt

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 10:37 p.m. in memory of Cerritos resident and Los
  Angeles City Fire Department Firefighter Jose “Joe” M. Perez.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

/s/Naresh Solanki
